title: Fresh Start
subtitle: 7 days to begin again
description: A week to reset your mornings and your mind. One short prayer a day before you scroll, plus one small step that makes room for God.
dailyTips: Pray before you check your phone this morning. Even one sentence counts.
Move one distracting app off your home screen today.
Tell God one thing you want to leave behind. Then leave it with him.
Read today’s verse twice: once quickly, once slowly. Notice what stands out the second time.
Pray for one person by name, then send them a kind message.
Charge your phone outside your bedroom tonight.
Look back at this week and thank God for one way he met you.

title: 21-Day Habit
subtitle: Make prayer your first tap
description: Three weeks to make prayer automatic. Pray at your gate every day, grow from 30 seconds to a few minutes, and let the habit carry you on the busy days.
dailyTips: Start small. A 30-second quick prayer is a win today.
Pick an anchor: pray right after your first coffee, shower or commute.
Notice the urge to scroll. Let it be your cue to pray.
Try the Guided style today: praise, confess, give thanks, then ask.
Pray out loud, even in a whisper. It helps your mind stay put.
Add one person to your prayer list.
One week down. Thank God for showing up, and thank yourself for showing up too.
Carry one short line with you all day: “God, I’m yours today.”
Write one line in your journal after you pray.
Pray with your eyes open on a walk. Talk to God about what you see.
Pray for someone you find difficult.
Read today’s verse, then pray it back to God in your own words.
Missed a day? Don’t start over in your head. Just pray now.
Two weeks in. Notice one thing that feels different.
Pray before a meal today, even if you’re out.
Put your phone face down for your whole prayer.
Ask God what he wants you to notice today, then pause and listen.
Pray for your neighbors, your city and your workplace.
Thank God for three things before you sleep.
Invite a friend to pray with you, or start a Prayer Circle.
You made it. Ask God which habit he wants to help you build next.

title: 40-Day Social Media Fast
subtitle: Less feed, more faith
description: Forty days to loosen social media’s grip. Pray every time you reach for the feed, cut back a little more each week, and fill the space with what actually feeds you.
dailyTips: Decide what this fast means for you: one app, all of them, or certain hours. Write it down.
Log out of one app today. A small speed bump goes a long way.
Every time you reach for the feed, pray one sentence instead.
Notice when you reach for your phone most: boredom, stress, loneliness. Tell God about it.
Turn off every notification you don’t truly need.
Replace your first scroll of the day with today’s verse.
One week in. Thank God for the minutes you got back, however many.
Move your social apps into a folder on your last screen.
Take a walk without your phone. Pray about whatever you see.
Call someone instead of watching their stories.
Keep your phone out of reach during meals today.
Read a chapter of one of the Gospels with the time you’d have scrolled.
When FOMO hits, pray for the people you feel you’re missing out on.
Two weeks in. What have you noticed about your mind? Tell God.
Try a phone-free evening: read, cook, rest or talk.
Write down three things you’ve done with your reclaimed time.
Pray for someone whose posts usually make you jealous.
Learn something offline today: a recipe, a song, a skill.
Let yourself be bored for five minutes. Let God meet you there.
Send someone an encouraging message, then close the app.
Three weeks in. Celebrate it. You’re further along than you think.
Ask God what he wants to fill this space with.
Spend ten minutes in silence. No phone, no music, just you and God.
Do something kind for a neighbor or coworker in real life.
Read a Psalm out loud before bed instead of scrolling.
Notice what you don’t miss. Thank God for the freedom.
Pray for the people who make the content you used to binge.
Four weeks in. Name one way your relationships feel different.
Plan a real-life hangout with a friend this week.
Write a prayer for your future self, for the day the fast ends.
Spend time outside and let creation be your feed today.
Ask God whether there’s an app you should leave behind for good.
Journal about the biggest change you’ve noticed so far.
Pray for each person who comes to mind today, as they come.
Five weeks in. Thank God for carrying you this far.
Set your boundaries for after the fast: times, places, limits.
Tell a friend what you’ve learned. Saying it out loud helps it stick.
Use some of your reclaimed time to serve someone today.
Write down how you want to use social media from now on, and why.
You finished. Come back slowly, keep your gate on, and keep praying first.

title: Pray for 30 People
subtitle: One person, every day
description: Thirty days, thirty people. Each day suggests someone new to pray for. Pray for them by name, and if you feel led, let them know you did.
dailyTips: Pray for someone in your family who’s on your mind today.
Pray for a friend you haven’t talked to in a while.
Pray for someone who taught you something that mattered.
Pray for a coworker or classmate you see often.
Pray for someone going through a hard season right now.
Pray for a neighbor, even one you barely know.
Pray for someone who is sick or in pain.
Pray for someone you find hard to love.
Pray for someone who is far from home.
Pray for a leader in your church or community.
Pray for someone who has prayed for you.
Pray for someone who is grieving.
Pray for someone starting something new: a job, a move, a family.
Pray for a friend who doesn’t know God yet.
Pray for someone who serves you: a barista, driver, nurse or teacher.
Pray for someone you need to forgive.
Pray for someone who is lonely.
Pray for a younger person who looks up to you.
Pray for someone older whose wisdom you value.
Pray for someone waiting on news: a test result, a job, an answer.
Pray for someone who made you laugh this week.
Pray for someone you follow online but have never met.
Pray for someone in your life who struggles with anxiety.
Pray for a friend who feels far from God right now.
Pray for someone who cares for others and is probably tired.
Pray for someone who hurt you.
Pray for someone you’ll meet later today.
Pray for someone serving far away: a missionary, aid worker or soldier.
Pray for your closest friend.
Pray for yourself. God loves you too. Pray for the person you’re becoming.

title: Gratitude Week
subtitle: Seven days of thank you
description: A week of noticing the good. Each day gives your thanks a different focus, so by day seven you see your life a little differently.
dailyTips: Thank God for three ordinary things you usually overlook.
Thank God for the people closest to you, one by one, by name.
Thank God for a hard thing that taught you something.
Thank God for your body, your health and your senses.
Thank God for a moment of beauty: something you saw, heard or tasted.
Write a thank-you message to someone and actually send it.
Thank God for who he is, not just for what he’s given.

title: Psalms Mornings
subtitle: Start each day in the Psalms
description: Two weeks of mornings in the Psalms, the Bible’s own prayer book. Read one before you scroll, then pray a line of it back to God.
dailyTips: Read Psalm 1. Ask God to plant you like a tree by the water.
Read Psalm 8. Look up at the sky today and remember how big God is.
Read Psalm 16. Pray its line about the path of life over your day.
Read Psalm 19. Notice one way creation points to God today.
Read Psalm 23. Pray it slowly, one line at a time.
Read Psalm 27. Tell God what you’re afraid of, then what you’re hoping for.
Read Psalm 34. Write down one way you’ve tasted God’s goodness lately.
Read Psalm 46. Spend one full minute being still before you check anything.
Read Psalm 51. Ask God for a clean heart and a fresh start.
Read Psalm 62. Wait quietly for God for a few slow breaths.
Read Psalm 91. Pray it over someone you love.
Read Psalm 103. List three of God’s kindnesses you don’t want to forget.
Read Psalm 121. Pray it before you leave the house today.
Read Psalm 139. Thank God that he knows you completely and stays.
